messages.content: Arizona is finally off my desk. I got invited to a veterinary diagnostics education summit in Indianapolis in mid-September, and I need help sketching flights and hotel before I say yes to the travel budget.
Sure. Send me the agenda anchors and what you know about the hotel setup. I’ll keep it to a short ranked plan rather than a giant fare dump.

Badge pickup and a reception are Monday evening. Supplier lab sessions start Tuesday morning. The final hands-on demo is Thursday and may run late enough that I’m worried about a Thursday flight home. I’d be flying Denver to Indianapolis.

That gives us three practical decisions: the Monday outbound, whether to come home Thursday night or Friday, and whether the conference hotel is worth taking over a better-amenity property. For DEN-IND, I’m seeing a Monday afternoon nonstop that arrives before the reception, plus a cheaper one-stop with a longer sit. The return can be done Thursday evening, but it looks dependent on how late that demo actually runs.
Give me the ranked version. I also want to know if the hot tub/pool/fitness trade-off is worth rideshares. I’m fine walking if the attached hotel is solid.

Flight ranking first: 1. Monday afternoon nonstop outbound plus Friday late-morning return. Best balance: simple outbound, no racing from the Thursday demo, and still only one extra hotel night. 2. Monday afternoon nonstop plus Thursday evening return. Cheaper on hotel nights, but only comfortable if the demo ends on time and you can go straight to the airport. 3. Cheaper one-stop outbound plus Friday return. It saves some money, but the connection is long enough that it eats the value unless the fare gap gets much bigger. I would not build this around a long connection just to save a modest amount.
No rental car unless there’s a real reason. What does Monday look like with the nonstop?

The nonstop is the clean one: leave Denver in the early-to-mid afternoon, land in Indianapolis a little before 6 local time, then take a rideshare straight to the convention-center area. If badge pickup runs into the evening, that should work with some buffer. The one-stop option lands later after a long connection, so it only makes sense if the reception timing is flexible or the fare difference becomes meaningful.
Badge pickup says 6 to 8 and the reception is roughly 6:30 to 8:30. I can miss the first few minutes. I don’t want a two-hour airport sit just to save $90.

Then I’d treat the Monday nonstop as the working outbound. Hotel ranking: 1. Convention-center block: strongest for the actual summit, guest score around the low 4s, attached or very easy walk, fitness room, indoor pool, no hot tub. 2. Suite property a short rideshare away: lower nightly rate, pool, hot tub, and fitness access, likely more comfortable for decompression, but you’ll add rideshares and lose the easy networking/drop-in convenience. 3. Airport hotel: only useful if you were arriving very late or staging for a flight; it does not help the summit days.
For a conference, attached usually wins. But if the block is mediocre I’d rather sleep at the suite property. Is the block above that basic business-hotel bar?

It looks acceptable rather than fancy. The useful points are the guest score, walkability, and not having to commute before the Tuesday labs. I’d want to confirm the room type, cancellation window, and whether they can note a quiet room. The amenity gap is real: indoor pool and fitness room are covered, hot tub is not. If hot tub recovery is the deciding factor, the suite property wins; if the summit schedule is the deciding factor, the block wins.
Can you put this into a decision version? What needs confirming before booking?

Yes. Before booking, confirm five things. First, badge pickup really stays open until at least 7:30 or 8, because that supports the Monday nonstop. Second, get the Thursday demo hard stop or expected end time; if it may run past 4:30, Friday return is the calmer choice. Third, check the hotel block cutoff, cancellation terms, quiet king availability, and fridge request. Fourth, ask whether any demo materials need shipping or if carrying them from the hotel is fine. Fifth, confirm there is no offsite lab location that would require a car. If all sessions are in or near the convention center, rideshares are enough.
What about Thursday return if I really want to be home Thursday? Is it impossible or just unpleasant?

Not impossible, but it’s a narrow lane. If the last workable flight leaves around early evening and the demo runs to 4:45, you’d need bags already handled, a quick exit from the session, a rideshare with no wait, and no security surprise. You’d also skip any debrief or late networking. If the demo ends closer to 4, it becomes more reasonable. If the demo timing is uncertain, Thursday night is the stress option.
I’d rather not bolt from the lab, but I also don’t love paying another night.

The extra night may partly wash out if the Friday return prices better than the Thursday evening flight. Even if it costs more overall, it buys you a clean demo finish, dinner without watching the clock, and a normal airport morning. For a summit where Thursday is the final hands-on piece, I’d lean Friday unless the coordinator confirms an earlier end.
Any reason United matters on this route?

On this route, United is relevant because it has one of the cleaner Denver nonstop options. I would use it if the timing and price stay close. I would not choose a United connection over a better nonstop or a much cleaner return; schedule simplicity is the driver here.
Okay. Tentative plan: Monday afternoon nonstop, probably Friday return, convention block unless the hot tub place is massively better. Can you give me the exact questions to send the coordinator?

Send this: Can you confirm Monday badge pickup hours and whether arriving around 6:15-6:30 is still fine? What is the realistic Thursday demo end time, and is attendance expected through the end? Are all Tuesday-Thursday sessions at the convention center or attached hotel area? For the hotel block, is there a quiet king available, what is the cancellation deadline, and can a fridge be requested? Are the indoor pool and fitness room open during the summit dates, and is it correct that there is no hot tub? Finally, should demo cases be carried in by attendees or shipped to the show desk? Once those answers come back, I’d be ready to book the Monday nonstop, decide Thursday versus Friday, and skip the car unless they name an offsite location.

messages.content: The Indianapolis coordinator answered. Badge pickup is open until 7:30 Monday, Tuesday starts at 8:30, and the Thursday demo could run until 4:45. The hotel block cutoff is coming up. Can we decide now?

Yes. With those times, the Monday afternoon nonstop is the clear outbound. It now prices close to the one-stop, so there’s no good reason to add the longer connection. For the return, Friday late morning is the cleaner pick; Thursday evening would require leaving almost straight from the demo. Hotel-wise, the block is still the convenience winner: guest score around 4.2, quiet king available to request, indoor pool and fitness room, but no hot tub.
Give me the booking version. I want the least annoying week, not an optimization over $50.

Book the Monday Denver to Indianapolis nonstop that lands before badge pickup closes. Pair it with a Friday late-morning Indianapolis to Denver return so Thursday can run long without turning into a sprint. Reserve the convention-center block before the cutoff, with quiet king, away from elevators or ice if possible, and fridge request. Skip the rental car unless your demo kit turns into more than you can reasonably roll into the hotel.
Yes, choose the nonstop on the outbound. Is Friday worth the extra hotel night?

Given the 4:45 possible demo end, yes. A Thursday flight means packed bags, no lingering questions, no post-demo conversation, and a direct dash to the airport. Friday gives you a normal close to the summit and a calmer morning ride to IND. If the fare difference is close, the extra hotel night is buying schedule control rather than luxury.
Okay, Friday. Hotel is my last hesitation. I keep thinking about the no hot tub piece, but walking to everything may matter more.

For this summit, I’d take the block. The suite property is the better wellness-amenity match because it has pool, hot tub, and fitness access, plus the lower rate. But the block keeps you steps from the 8:30 start, badge pickup, reception, and any hallway networking. Since the block still has the pool and fitness room and a decent guest score, the missing hot tub is the trade-off I’d accept here.
Book the block if it’s cancelable until at least a couple days before arrival. Add quiet room away from elevators and a fridge if that’s allowed.

I’ll reserve the block under those terms if available: quiet king, away from elevators/ice, fridge requested, Monday evening arrival noted. I’ll also keep the suite property as the backup until the block confirmation and cancellation language are clear.
Do I need a rental car? I’ll have one demo kit but not a full booth.

No rental car for this version. Airport rideshare to the hotel, then walking for the summit days. Parking would be wasted money, and downtown driving adds more friction than value. If the demo kit gets heavy or awkward, shipping it to the show desk is better than renting a car just to move one case.
Please also make sure I’m not stuck in a middle seat.
Window or aisle for these legs if both are available?
Window if it’s open. Aisle only if the only window is in the last row.

Got it. I’ll book the Monday nonstop outbound, the Friday late-morning return, select or request window seats that are not last-row seats, reserve the convention-center block with the quiet king and fridge notes, and leave the car off the plan. Open follow-ups after booking: save the hotel cancellation deadline, watch for schedule changes, and ask the coordinator for demo-kit shipping instructions if the case gets any bulkier.

messages.content: Six days out for Indianapolis. I got a schedule-change email, and the seat map looks weird. Can you sanity-check the last logistics?

Yes. The outbound moved 28 minutes later, but it still works for badge pickup if you go straight from IND to the hotel by rideshare. Do not wait around for a shuttle. The aircraft swap is why the window seat disappeared; I’ll recheck for another acceptable window and avoid moving you into a middle seat.
I also have one demo case. The convention email says the loading zone is going to be a mess Monday.

Then ship that case to the show desk if they’ll accept it. Ask for the label format, receiving hours, and pickup location. It will be much easier than managing a case through airport rideshare pickup and a crowded hotel arrival.
Hotel confirmed the quiet king note and the fridge request. Same story: pool and fitness room, no hot tub.
Good. That keeps the hotel plan intact. Monday arrival should be rideshare, check in, drop your bag, then badge pickup before 7:30. If the flight slips at all, badge pickup comes before dinner.
What time should I leave for DEN?

Aim to be at DEN about two hours before the new departure. If the flight is now just after 2, leave home around 11:15 to 11:30. Since the demo case should ship separately, you can keep the airport day to your carry-on and laptop bag.
And dinner? I won’t have bandwidth for anything complicated after that later arrival.

Keep it simple: hotel bar or a nearby casual place after badge pickup, with an airport snack as the backup if the arrival slips. I’ll recheck seats at the 24-hour mark, confirm the demo-case shipping instructions, and set the Friday plan as rideshare to IND around 8:45-9:00 for the late-morning flight home.
